title: Contaminated event window: confounding news during event period

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
To decompose the market reaction and isolate the acquisition effect from the confounding earnings news, we will use an Event Study approach. The key assumption is that the earnings surprise can be controlled for by including it as a regressor in the analysis. This approach allows us to partial out the effect of the earnings surprise on the stock return, thereby isolating the effect of the acquisition announcement. The main equation will be a modified version of the standard market model, which includes an additional regressor for the earnings surprise.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(broom)

# Read the CSV file
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s18_data.csv")

# Filter the data for event day 0 (announcement day)
announcement_day_data <- data %>% 
  filter(event_day == 0)

# Run the AR regression for each stock
regressions <- announcement_day_data %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  do(model = lm(ret ~ mkt_ret + eps_surprise + beta, data = .))

# Print the coefficients
tidy(regressions, model) %>% 
  mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 4) %>% 
  select(term, estimate)

# Estimate the average acquisition effect by taking the mean of the intercepts
acquisition_effect <- tidy(regressions, model) %>% 
  filter(term == "(Intercept)") %>% 
  pull(estimate) %>% 
  mean()

print(paste("Average acquisition effect: ", round(acquisition_effect, 4)))

# Basic robustness check: re-run the analysis with different specifications
robustness_check <- announcement_day_data %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  do(model = lm(ret ~ mkt_ret + eps_surprise, data = .))

tidy(robustness_check, model) %>% 
  mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 4) %>% 
  select(term, estimate)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect a positive acquisition effect, as the market typically reacts positively to acquisition announcements. However, the magnitude will depend on various factors such as the industry, firm size, and type of acquisition. Since we are controlling for the earnings surprise, the acquisition effect should be less biased by the confounding news. The coefficient on the intercept term in the regression equation represents the average acquisition effect, and we expect it to be positive. The exact magnitude will depend on the data, but a reasonable estimate might be in the range of 1-5%, depending on the market's reaction to similar acquisition announcements in the past.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study with confound adjustment — regress AR on eps_surprise + acquisition dummy
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: After controlling for earnings surprise, acquisition announcement generates negative AR
